Topics.Title: The PreseMaker Hierarchy Overview
Topics.Summary: Introduces the overall organizational structure of PreseMaker, explaining how courses, modules, topics, and generated materials fit together as a unified system.

Elements.Title: What Is PreseMaker?
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker is an e-learning authoring tool built around a clear, layered organizational system for creating and managing educational content.
Elements.Notes: Understanding PreseMaker as a system—rather than just a single tool—helps learners appreciate why the hierarchy exists and how it supports scalable course creation.

Items.Text: PreseMaker is designed to help authors structure, generate, and store e-learning materials in a consistent and repeatable way.
The entire platform revolves around a defined hierarchy that keeps content organized from the broadest level down to individual generated assets.

Elements.Title: The Four Levels of the Hierarchy
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker organizes content into nested levels: Courses contain Modules, Modules contain Topics, and Topics contain Subtopics. The materials PreseMaker produces are outputs generated from these levels.
Elements.Notes: Think of the hierarchy like nested containers — each level holds and gives meaning to the level below it.

Items.Text: A Course is the top-level container, representing a complete learning program or subject area.
A Module sits inside a Course and groups related instructional content around a specific theme or unit.
A Topic lives within a Module and represents a single, focused lesson or concept.

A Subtopic sits within a Topic, dividing a lesson into finer points; the materials PreseMaker generates (such as slides, notes, or quizzes) are outputs produced from these levels, not a level of their own.

Elements.Title: How Courses Serve as the Top-Level Container
Elements.BodyText: A Course is the broadest organizational unit in PreseMaker, providing the overarching framework under which all other content is grouped.
Elements.Notes: A single PreseMaker project may contain one or many Courses, depending on the scope of the author's work.

Items.Text: Courses define the overall subject, audience, or program that the content belongs to.
All Modules, Topics, and Generated Materials ultimately trace back to and are organized under a parent Course.

Elements.Title: Modules as Thematic Groupings
Elements.BodyText: Modules break a Course into manageable sections, each focused on a distinct theme, unit, or instructional goal.
Elements.Notes: Modules allow authors to plan and build content incrementally rather than tackling an entire Course at once.

Items.Text: Each Module contains one or more Topics, all of which relate to the Module's central theme.
Modules help learners navigate a Course by providing clear, logical boundaries between different areas of content.
Authors can add, reorder, or update Modules independently without disrupting the rest of the Course structure.

Elements.Title: Topics as the Core Instructional Unit
Elements.BodyText: Topics are where individual lessons are defined; each Topic represents a single, focused concept or learning objective within a Module.
Elements.Notes: Topics are the direct source from which PreseMaker generates content assets, making them the most actionable level of the hierarchy.

Items.Text: A Topic typically includes a title, a summary, and source content that PreseMaker uses to produce materials.
Each Topic is self-contained, allowing it to be edited, regenerated, or reused without affecting sibling Topics.
The specificity of a Topic directly influences the relevance and quality of the materials PreseMaker generates from it.

Elements.Title: Generated Materials as the Output Layer
Elements.BodyText: Generated Materials are the tangible content assets that PreseMaker produces from a Topic, such as presentation slides, speaker notes, or assessments.
Elements.Notes: Because Generated Materials are derived from Topics, updating a Topic's source content allows authors to regenerate fresh materials without starting from scratch.

Items.Text: Generated Materials represent the final deliverables that learners or instructors will actually use.
Each set of Generated Materials is tied to a specific Topic, keeping outputs traceable back through the full hierarchy.
PreseMaker stores Generated Materials in an organized file structure on the author's computer, ensuring full ownership and accessibility.

Elements.Title: The Hierarchy as a Unified System
Elements.BodyText: The four levels of the PreseMaker hierarchy are not isolated layers — they work together as a unified system where each level informs and supports the others.
Elements.Notes: Viewing the hierarchy as a system rather than a simple folder structure helps authors make better decisions about how to organize and scope their content.

Items.Text: Changes or additions at any level of the hierarchy are reflected in the context of the levels above and below it.
The unified structure ensures that content remains consistent, navigable, and easy to maintain over time.
Understanding how Courses, Modules, Topics, and Subtopics relate to one another — and how PreseMaker generates materials from them — is foundational to using PreseMaker effectively.

Topics.Title: Understanding Courses and Modules
Topics.Summary: Explores the relationship between courses and modules, clarifying how modules serve as the primary building blocks organized within a course.

Elements.Title: What Is a Course?
Elements.BodyText: A course is the top-level container in PreseMaker, representing the broadest organizational unit for a subject or learning program.
Elements.Notes: Think of a course as the overall wrapper — for example, 'Introduction to Digital Marketing' — under which all related content lives.

Items.Text: A course defines the overall subject area or learning goal that a learner is working toward.
All modules, topics, and generated materials ultimately belong to a single parent course.
Creating a course is the first step before any content can be organized or produced in PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: What Is a Module?
Elements.BodyText: A module is the primary building block within a course, representing a focused section or unit of instruction.
Elements.Notes: For example, a course on Digital Marketing might contain modules such as 'SEO Basics,' 'Social Media Strategy,' and 'Email Campaigns.'

Items.Text: Modules break a course into manageable, thematically grouped sections of content.
Each module sits one level below the course and one level above individual topics or content items.
A single course can contain multiple modules, allowing complex subjects to be organized into logical chunks.

Elements.Title: The Parent-Child Relationship Between Courses and Modules
Elements.BodyText: Courses and modules share a hierarchical parent-child relationship, where the course acts as the parent and modules act as its children.
Elements.Notes: This hierarchy ensures that content is always contextually anchored — a module cannot exist independently; it must belong to a course.

Items.Text: A course can contain one or many modules, but each module belongs to exactly one course.
This relationship keeps related instructional content grouped together and easy to navigate.
Understanding this hierarchy is essential for knowing where to add, edit, or find content within PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: Why Modules Are the Primary Building Blocks
Elements.BodyText: Modules are considered the primary building blocks of a course because they are the main units through which instructional content is structured and delivered.
Elements.Notes: While courses define the 'what' at a high level, modules define 'how' that subject is divided into teachable segments.

Items.Text: Modules provide the structural framework that keeps a course organized and pedagogically sound.
All finer-grained content elements — such as topics and generated materials — are housed within modules.
Designing a course effectively begins with planning its modules, as they determine the learner's path through the material.

Elements.Title: Organizing Modules Within a Course
Elements.BodyText: Modules within a course can be arranged in a deliberate sequence to guide learners through content in a logical and progressive order.
Elements.Notes: For instance, foundational modules might be placed first, with advanced or applied modules following later in the course sequence.

Items.Text: The order of modules within a course reflects the intended learning progression for the subject.
Instructors can structure modules to build on one another, supporting scaffolded learning.
A well-organized set of modules ensures learners experience content coherently rather than in isolated fragments.

Topics.Title: Topics and Generated Materials
Topics.Summary: Examines how topics nest within modules and how PreseMaker generates content materials from those topics, connecting structure to output.

Elements.Title: Topics as Building Blocks Within Modules
Elements.BodyText: Topics are the smallest structural unit within a module, each representing a focused concept or skill area.
Elements.Notes: Think of a module as a chapter and topics as the individual sections within that chapter, each covering one distinct idea.

Items.Text: Each module contains one or more topics that collectively cover the module's overall subject matter.
Topics are sequenced within a module to create a logical learning progression.
Keeping each topic tightly focused ensures generated materials remain clear and coherent.

Elements.Title: How Topics Nest Inside Modules
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker organizes topics in a hierarchical relationship, where every topic belongs to exactly one parent module.
Elements.Notes: This nesting means that editing or reorganizing a module directly affects which topics — and therefore which generated materials — are associated with it.

Items.Text: A topic cannot exist independently; it must always be assigned to a module.
Multiple topics can be nested under a single module, allowing complex subjects to be broken into manageable pieces.
The nesting structure is reflected in how PreseMaker displays and navigates content during authoring.

Elements.Title: From Topic to Generated Content
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker uses the information defined in a topic — its title, summary, and source content — to automatically generate learning materials.
Elements.Notes: The quality and specificity of the topic definition directly influences the relevance and accuracy of the generated output.

Items.Text: Each topic acts as the input source that drives PreseMaker's content generation process.
Generated materials are scoped to their topic, meaning output stays focused on that topic's defined subject matter.
Changing a topic's details will affect what gets generated when content is produced or regenerated.

Elements.Title: Types of Materials Generated from Topics
Elements.BodyText: For each topic, PreseMaker can produce a variety of content elements that together form the learner-facing material.
Elements.Notes: These materials collectively build out the instructional content that learners experience when moving through a module.

Items.Text: Generated materials may include slides, explanatory text, key points, notes, and assessment items tied to the topic.
Each material type serves a distinct instructional purpose, from introducing concepts to reinforcing and testing understanding.
All generated materials for a topic are linked back to that topic within the course structure.

Elements.Title: The Structural Chain: Course → Module → Topic → Materials
Elements.BodyText: Understanding the full hierarchy helps authors see how a top-level course ultimately produces granular learning content through a series of nested relationships.
Elements.Notes: Visualizing this chain helps authors make intentional decisions about where to place content and how to organize their courses effectively.

Items.Text: A course contains modules, modules contain topics, and topics produce generated materials — each level depends on the one above it.
This chain ensures that all generated materials are always traceable back to their source topic, module, and course.
Structural changes at any level, such as moving or renaming a module, cascade down to affect the topics and materials beneath it.

Elements.Title: Connecting Structure to Output
Elements.BodyText: The relationship between topics and generated materials is what bridges course design with the actual learner experience in PreseMaker.
Elements.Notes: A well-structured set of topics leads to coherent, well-scoped generated materials, making the authoring investment in structure directly visible in the final output.

Items.Text: Every piece of generated output corresponds to a specific topic, making it easy to identify where content came from.
Authors can refine or regenerate materials for individual topics without affecting content generated from other topics.
The structural connection between topics and materials supports consistent, organized course delivery.

Topics.Title: How PreseMaker Stores Files on Your Computer
Topics.Summary: Describes where and how PreseMaker saves files locally on the author's computer, ensuring users understand file locations and ownership of their work.

Elements.Title: Local Storage: Where PreseMaker Saves Your Files
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker saves all generated course materials directly to your local computer rather than storing them exclusively in the cloud.
Elements.Notes: This means your files are accessible even without an internet connection, giving you full control over your content at all times.

Items.Text: Files are written to a designated folder on your local drive each time content is generated or updated.
The local storage approach ensures that your work stays on your own computer and does not rely on any online service's servers or your account status.
You can navigate to the storage location using your operating system's file explorer just like any other folder on your computer.

Elements.Title: Default File Location and Folder Structure
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker organizes saved files into a predictable folder hierarchy that mirrors the course-module-content structure used inside the application.
Elements.Notes: For example, a course titled 'Sales Training' might create a top-level folder of the same name, with subfolders for each module and individual files for each topic or content element.

Items.Text: A root PreseMaker folder is created in a standard location such as your Documents directory during initial setup.
Inside the root folder, each course is represented by its own named subfolder, keeping projects separated and easy to find.
Module and content files are nested within their respective course folders, preserving the logical hierarchy you see in the application.

Elements.Title: File Formats Used by PreseMaker
Elements.BodyText: Generated materials are saved in common, widely supported file formats so they can be opened, edited, and shared without requiring special software.
Elements.Notes: Using standard formats reduces dependency on PreseMaker itself and makes it straightforward to hand off content to colleagues or import it into other tools.

Items.Text: Presentation files are typically saved in formats compatible with major presentation applications, such as .pptx.
Text lessons are saved as HTML (interactive or printable) and Markdown, presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files, and quiz banks export to the QTI and WPProQuiz formats.
Because the formats are non-proprietary, you are never locked into PreseMaker to access or modify your own work.

Elements.Title: Ownership and Access Rights to Your Files
Elements.BodyText: All files saved by PreseMaker belong entirely to the user; the application does not retain ownership or impose usage restrictions on generated content.
Elements.Notes: This is an important distinction from subscription-based platforms that may restrict export or reuse of content created within their environment.

Items.Text: You retain full intellectual property rights over any content you create and generate through PreseMaker.
Files can be copied, moved, shared, or deleted at any time without needing to interact with the PreseMaker application.
There are no license flags or digital rights management controls embedded in the saved files.

Elements.Title: Locating and Verifying Your Saved Files
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker provides straightforward ways to confirm where a file has been saved and to open its containing folder directly from within the application.
Elements.Notes: Being able to verify file location immediately after generation helps prevent confusion about which version of a file is the most current.

Items.Text: A file path or 'Show in Folder' option is typically displayed after content is generated, allowing instant navigation to the saved file.
You can also check the application's settings or preferences panel to view or change the default save location at any time.
Verifying the file location before closing a project is a good habit that prevents accidental data loss.

Elements.Title: Managing and Backing Up Your PreseMaker Files
Elements.BodyText: Because files live on your local computer, it is the user's responsibility to back up and manage those files to prevent accidental loss.
Elements.Notes: Integrating the PreseMaker output folder into an existing backup routine—such as cloud sync or an external drive backup—is the simplest way to protect your work.

Items.Text: Regularly copying your PreseMaker folder to an external drive or cloud storage service protects against hardware failure.
Version control practices, such as duplicating a file before making major edits, help preserve previous iterations of your content.
Deleting a file from your computer permanently removes it, because PreseMaker keeps no server-side copy — it is a local desktop application with no backend.

Topics.Title: Accessing and Owning Your Work
Topics.Summary: Reinforces that authors retain full ownership of all generated content and explains how to reliably locate and manage their files at any time.

Elements.Title: You Own Everything You Create
Elements.BodyText: All content generated through PreseMaker belongs entirely to you, the author, with no restrictions or platform lock-in.
Elements.Notes: This means you are free to use, edit, share, or repurpose your generated materials however you choose, outside of PreseMaker if needed.

Items.Text: Ownership is retained by the creator from the moment content is generated.
PreseMaker does not claim rights over any materials produced using the platform.
You may distribute or modify your generated files without seeking additional permissions.

Elements.Title: Where PreseMaker Stores Your Files
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker saves all generated content to a designated location on your local computer, making files easy to find and manage.
Elements.Notes: Knowing the default storage location prevents confusion when looking for files after a session ends.

Items.Text: Files are stored locally on your device, not exclusively in a remote cloud system.
A default folder path is assigned by PreseMaker during installation or first use.
Understanding this path ensures you can navigate directly to your work at any time.

Elements.Title: Locating Your Files at Any Time
Elements.BodyText: PreseMaker provides consistent, reliable methods for finding your saved content whenever you need it.
Elements.Notes: Using the platform's built-in file navigation alongside your operating system's file explorer gives you two complementary ways to access your work.

Items.Text: You can access saved files directly through PreseMaker's interface using the course-module-content hierarchy.
Files can also be located by browsing to the designated storage folder through your operating system's file explorer.
Content is organized by course and module, reflecting the structure you built inside PreseMaker.

Elements.Title: Managing and Organizing Your Generated Content
Elements.BodyText: Keeping your files organized ensures long-term accessibility and makes it easier to revisit or build upon previous work.
Elements.Notes: Consistent naming and folder organization habits reduce time spent searching for specific materials later.

Items.Text: PreseMaker structures saved files to mirror the course-module-topic hierarchy, aiding natural organization.
You can rename, move, or archive files using standard operating system tools without affecting the platform.
Regularly reviewing your storage folder helps you stay aware of what has been generated and what may need updating.

Elements.Title: Accessing Your Work Across Sessions
Elements.BodyText: Your generated content persists between sessions, so progress and completed materials are never lost when you close the application.
Elements.Notes: This persistence is especially valuable for long-term projects that span multiple working sessions.

Items.Text: Files saved during one session remain available the next time you open PreseMaker or browse your storage folder.
There is no need to re-generate content unless you intentionally choose to update or replace it.
Consistent local storage means your work is accessible even without an active internet connection.
